title: Patch: a fork screen saves each deal as it finishes and picks up where it stopped, so a screen cut off part-way loses nothing
thread:
**Issue #4607 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4607: Patch: a fork screen saves each deal as it finishes and picks up where it stopped, so a screen cut off part-way loses nothing
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

A change to the practice AI is meant to be measured before it ships. The measurement that suits most AI changes plays the old and the new AI from every spot where they would choose differently and counts which choice wins more. One such run takes three to four hours on a four-core machine, and it keeps every result in memory until the very end. When the run stops early, because the bot's time ran out or a cloud machine was taken back, the hours are lost and nothing is printed. After this change, each finished deal is written to a file as soon as it is done. Running the same command again on the same file plays only the deals still missing, and prints exactly what one uninterrupted run would have printed. The night bot can then finish a measurement over two of its runs, so AI changes arrive with a measured result instead of none. Players see nothing; the maintainer sees AI pull requests that carry their measurement.

## Why

- Every idea for the AI now goes "through the night bot as an issue with a measured acceptance" (`training/improve.md:7`), since the improve, unban and learn lanes are stopped or retired.
- A fork screen does not fit a bot run. #4448's two screens took 3 h 7 min and 4 h 0 min on a 4-core Xeon, about 12 and 16 core-hours. "Neither fits a bot's model call (150 minutes), and a fork screen prints nothing until its tally and cannot resume." The first run of #4448's `turn_hook` screen died 3 hours in, when its cloud session was reclaimed (`training/improve.md:170-176`).
- AI changes therefore ship unmeasured:
  - #4447's fork screen "did not finish in the bot's run: stopped after 2 hours, nothing printed", so `AI_SEARCH.replay_fill_steps` ships at 0 untested (`crates/ai/src/config.rs:226-229`).
  - R4515000 shipped with "No screen was played" (`config.rs:1070`).
  - #4448 first went back to a person: "the bot could not build it: run the issue's two fork screens on a machine of your own".
- The cause is in `crates/tools/src/fork_screen.rs:609-683`. `run` holds the trunk, the forks and the edges in memory across every batch and writes nothing until the last one ends.
- Yet each deal is independent and small:
  - It is set up from its number alone (`trunk_setups`, `:565`).
  - The tally reads only each arm's win and fault (`ArmOutcome`, `:199`).
  - So a deal's results fit on one short line, and deals can be played in any order.
- The bot's harness pushes a cut-off build's work to its branch and continues it in the next run (`bot/README.md`, Handing work over). A save file in the worktree therefore survives the cut.

## Proposal

- **The flag.** `cargo jackioh arena --a … --b … --set improve-dev --forks --save <file>`. Without `--save`, nothing changes.
- **The header.** The file opens with one line naming the set, `--games`, `--extend`, the budget, `FORK_ROLLOUTS`, `FORK_MAX_PER_GAME`, the catalog version, and each agent's label and `agent info` answer.
- **One line per deal.** A deal is played as a unit: its trunk game, then its forks' arms. Deals still run in parallel, and arms still assemble in `(deal, fork, pair, arm)` order. When a deal is done, one JSON line is appended and flushed. It holds:
  - the deal number;
  - its duel line and its game record;
  - its forks (seat, move, both actions);
  - each arm's win and fault.

  A torn last line, left by a killed process, is dropped and its deal is played again.
- **Resuming.** Run again on the same file, the screen:
  1. refuses a header that differs, naming the field;
  2. plays its first saved deal's trunk again and refuses the file unless the trunk's hash and its forks match. This is one game, and it catches a rebuilt binary of another AI;
  3. plays only the deals the file is missing.

  `--extend` takes its batch stops from the saved deals and the new ones together, so it stops where one run would.
- **The output.** The tally, the duel lines and the records come from every deal's line in deal order. A screen played in pieces prints the tally line an uninterrupted one prints, byte for byte. Duel lines carry decision times, so they are the saved ones.
- **No second reads.** A finished save (every deal in, or `--extend` stopped) prints its tally again and plays nothing. Its size is fixed in the header, so a screen cannot be grown after its tally was read (R850001's rule against second reads, R4319000).
- **Docs.** `training/improve.md`, A screen, tells a bot's builder three things:
  - pass `--save` with a path inside its worktree, so its harness carries the file into a continued run;
  - after a cut, run the same command again;
  - record the tally in the knob's config comment as today, and remove the file before it finishes.

  Out of scope: the deal screen (`--set` without `--forks`, 25 to 45 minutes) already fits a bot run and is left alone.

## Where it lands

- `crates/tools/src/fork_screen.rs`: per-deal units, the save, the resume and the identity check.
- `crates/tools/src/arena.rs`: `Args.save`.
- `training/improve.md` (A screen), `training/README.md` (The arena and the agent), `crates/tools/README.md`, `docs/v0.3.0/SURFACE.md` (the arena paragraph of §14).
- A ruling in the issue's block beside R4397000 (SPEC §9.9, the training lanes' screens), proven in `fork_screen.rs`, with its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/<issue>.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

All tests use a scripted probe and the tests' budget, as `fork_screen.rs`'s tests do.

- [ ] A save cut back to its first deal's line, as a killed run leaves it, is resumed. The resume plays only the missing deal and prints a tally line byte-identical to an uninterrupted run's. Its file ends with the same deal lines.
- [ ] A save whose last line is torn resumes with that deal played again.
- [ ] Resuming with any of these differing is refused before any game is played, naming what differs: another candidate (a scripted probe that differs at another move), another control, set, `--games`, `--extend` or budget.
- [ ] A finished save, run again, plays no game and prints the same tally.
- [ ] A unit test holds `--extend`'s next batch to the live forks of the saved deals and the new ones together.
- [ ] Without `--save`, every existing test in `fork_screen.rs` and `arena.rs` passes unchanged. The daily thread-count test still holds.
- [ ] The docs above describe the flag and the resume. `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.

## Size and risks

Medium: about seven files, most of the code in `fork_screen.rs`. No AI decision, engine rule or game changes.

Risks:
- Playing a deal as one unit can leave cores idle at a batch's tail, since deals differ in length. Interleaving the arms of several deals on rayon, as today, avoids that.
- Rollout tests are slow (R4397000's byte-identity test is daily, #4462). The per-pull-request tests keep to one or two trunk deals with a scripted fork late in the game.
- A save holds a deal's game record (about 2 KB), so a 200-deal save is about half a megabyte. That is why the builder removes it before finishing rather than committing it as a record.

Area: `ai` (`suggestions.areas`).

## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/45231445005)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`cargo jackioh arena --set improve-dev --forks --save <file>` writes one JSON header line then one JSON line per finished deal (trunk game plus its forks' arms), flushed at once, so a killed run loses at most unfinished deals. Running the same command again refuses a mismatched file by field name, replays the first saved deal's trunk once as an identity check, plays only missing deals, and prints byte-for-byte what one uninterrupted run prints. Without `--save` the screen behaves exactly as today. A new ruling beside R4397000 and doc updates in the three training/arena docs complete it.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/tools/src/fork_screen.rs` | change | `FORK_SAVE_VERSION`, `SaveHeader`/`DealLine` types, `play_deal`, `append_deal_line`, `load_save`, `check_header`, `identity_check`, `edges_of`, `tally_from_lines`, `next_batch`, `resume_save`, save branch of `run`; `r4607000_*` tests |
| `crates/tools/src/arena.rs` | change | `Args.save: Option<PathBuf>`, `--save`-needs-`--forks` guard in `run`; one guard test |
| `spec/rulings/R4607000.md` | new | Ruling R4607000 (first free in issue 4607's block), `proven_in: crates/tools/src/fork_screen.rs` |
| `spec/pending/4607.md` | new | The §11 paragraph for R4607000 |
| `training/improve.md` | change | `### A screen`: `--save` instructions for a bot builder |
| `training/README.md` | change | The arena and the agent: fork bullet gains `--save` |
| `crates/tools/README.md` | change | Arena row: `--save <path>` in usage plus one sentence (acceptance test reads every `--flag` from this row) |
| `docs/v0.3.0/SURFACE.md` | change | §14.2 usage line and `--forks` paragraph gain `--save` |

Must not touch: `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `crates/engine/`, `crates/cards/`, `crates/ai/`, `apps/`, `e2e/`, `spec/11-rulings.md`, `spec/INDEX.md`, `spec/CARDS.md`, and the deal-screen (`--set` without `--forks`) path in `arena.rs`. Governing spec: §9.9, R4397000, R850001, R4319000, R1489000.

## Steps

1. `crates/tools/src/arena.rs`, `Args`: add `#[arg(long)] pub save: Option<PathBuf>` with doc comment "R4607000: the fork screen's save file". At the top of `run()`, before the `forks` dispatch, bail when `args.save.is_some() && !args.forks` (`"arena: --save resumes only the fork screen, so it needs --forks"`). The deal-screen path stays untouched.
2. `crates/tools/src/fork_screen.rs`, types: add `pub(crate) const FORK_SAVE_VERSION: u32 = 1` (CLAUDE.md rule 9). Add `SaveHeader { v, set: String, games: i32, extend: bool, budget: SearchBudget, fork_rollouts: usize, fork_max_per_game: usize, catalog: String, a_label, b_label: String, a_info, b_info: crate::agent::AgentInfo }` and `DealLine { deal: i32, duel: String, record: Option<GameRecord>, hash: String, forks: Vec<SavedFork{seat, at_move, candidate, control}>, probe_faults: Vec<String>, arms: Vec<SavedArm{won, fault}> }`, all Serialize+Deserialize, camelCase. Per-fork arms are stored in `(pair, arm)` slot order (cand, ctl per pair). `GameRecord` needs importing from `jackioh_engine`.
3. Same file, `play_deal(game: &ArenaGame, probe: Probe) -> anyhow::Result<DealLine>`: run `play_game_probed`, build the one deal's jobs, run existing `play_forks` (keeps `(deal, fork, pair, arm)` assembly), flatten outcomes to `SavedArm` in slot order, then `duel: duel_line(outcome, replays(outcome)?)`, `record: game_record(outcome)?`, `hash: outcome.hash`. Extract the cand/ctl win-count loop from `play_forks` into `fn edge_of_slots(won: &[bool]) -> f64` and reuse it in `edges_of` (step 5) so saved and live edges cannot diverge.
4. Same file, file I/O: `append_deal_line(path, line)` opens with append+create, writes one JSON line, flushes. `load_save(path)` reads the header plus deal lines into a `BTreeMap<i32, DealLine>`; a last line that fails to parse is dropped with an `eprintln` warning (the torn line); a failing non-last line or a duplicate deal number is an error naming the line. `check_header(header, args, a, b, budget, deals)` compares set, games, extend, budget, `FORK_ROLLOUTS`, `FORK_MAX_PER_GAME`, catalog version, both labels and both agent infos, bailing with the differing field's name (e.g. `"arena: save <file> is for --games 200, not 400"`).
5. Same file, resume core: `identity_check(game, probe, saved)` plays the first saved deal's trunk and bails naming `trunk hash` or `forks` unless hash and every fork's seat, `at_move`, and both actions' `fork_key` match. `edges_of(lines in deal order) -> Vec<ForkEdge>` recomputes edges from saved arms. `tally_from_lines(header, lines) -> (String tally_json, Vec<String> duel_lines, Vec<GameRecord>)` via existing `fork_tally`, in deal order. `next_batch(games_done, live, extend, initial_deals) -> Option<(first, len)>`: first batch `(1, initial_deals)`; later batches only when `extend`, `None` when `screen_done(live, games_done)`, else `(games_done+1, min(SCREEN_EXTEND_DEALS, SCREEN_MAX_GAMES-games_done))`. `--extend` totals count saved plus new deals together.
6. Same file, `resume_save(path, expected: &SaveHeader, base: &str, b: &Entrant, initial_deals, extend, make_probe: &dyn Fn(&ArenaGame) -> anyhow::Result<Probe>) -> anyhow::Result<SaveReport>`: load, `check_header`, finished check (every target deal present, and with `extend` also `screen_done`), returning a re-read of the file with zero games played when finished; else `identity_check` on the first saved deal, then per-batch `par_iter` over missing deals calling `play_deal`, appending each finished line immediately under a file mutex with flush (completion order; readers sort by deal), looping on `next_batch`. `SaveReport` carries tally JSON, duel lines, records, and a games-played count.
7. Same file, `run()`: after the existing arg checks and entrant setup, branch on `args.save`. `None`: today's loop verbatim. `Some(path)`: build the expected header (budget = `AI_GATE_BUDGET`, the trunk setups' budget; deals = requested count), create-or-resume the file (write header when creating), call `resume_save` with `|game| Probe::for_game(&args.a, game.self_budget, game.n)`, then print duel lines, tally, and a `"<n> deals in <file>"` line to stdout exactly like the `--out` branch minus record appending (the save file is the record store; never re-append records). Every `--save` run prints this same shape, so piece-wise and uninterrupted runs match byte for byte.
8. Ruling + docs: write `spec/rulings/R4607000.md` (`cards: "§9.9, R4397000, R850001, R4319000, R1489000, issue #4607"`, Hearthstone-has-no-counterpart line as R4397000 does) and `spec/pending/4607.md` (the `**[[R4607000]] … (issue #4607, …)**` paragraph). `training/improve.md` `### A screen`, after the fork-screen paragraph: pass `--save` at a path inside the worktree, rerun the same command after a cut, record the tally in the knob's config comment, delete the file before finishing. One sentence each in `training/README.md` (fork bullet), `crates/tools/README.md` (arena row usage ` [--save <path>]` plus behavior), `docs/v0.3.0/SURFACE.md` (§14.2 usage + fork paragraph: header contents, resume, identity check, finished-save reprint).

## Tests

All in `crates/tools/src/fork_screen.rs` tests mod, scripted probe differing only at `at_move == 1` (a late fork, cheap) at `TEST_BUDGET` over 1–2 `trunk_game` deals, driving the factored fns (never the CLI):

- `r4607000_resume_after_cut_prints_the_same_tally`: uninterrupted header+2 lines vs cut file (header+deal 1) resumed through `resume_save`; assert tally strings byte-equal and sorted deal lines equal.
- `r4607000_a_torn_last_line_is_played_again`: deal-1 line plus a truncated fragment; resume replays deal 2 and the tally equals the uninterrupted one.
- `r4607000_resume_refuses_a_changed_header_before_any_game`: mutate each of set, games, extend, budget, catalog, labels, infos, fork constants; each errors naming the field, file bytes unchanged, probe factory called zero times.
- `r4607000_a_different_candidate_fails_the_identity_game`: same header, probe differing at another move; exactly one trunk game played, error names `forks`.
- `r4607000_a_finished_save_plays_nothing_and_reprints_its_tally`: full file resumed; zero games, same tally, file unchanged.
- `r4607000_extend_counts_saved_and_new_live_forks_together`: pure `next_batch` cases (saved 200 games/19 live continues at 201; 20 live stops; cap respected).
- `crates/tools/src/arena.rs`: `save_needs_forks`: `Args` with `save` and `forks: false` errors on `--forks`.

Commands: `cargo test -p jackioh-tools fork_screen`, `cargo test -p jackioh-tools arena`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo jackioh spec check`. Existing `fork_screen.rs`/`arena.rs` tests must pass unchanged; the daily thread-count test is not modified.

## Done when

- [ ] Cut-resume prints a byte-identical tally with the same deal lines; torn tail replayed; header mismatches refused by field before any game; behaviorally different candidate refused after exactly one identity game; finished save replays nothing and reprints.
- [ ] `--extend` batches stop on saved plus new live forks together; no-`--save` output and all existing tests unchanged.
- [ ] New tests fail without the change (cut-resume has no resume path; refusal/identity paths missing).
- [ ] Docs above describe flag and resume; `cargo jackioh spec check`, fmt, and clippy pass.

## Risks

- Per-deal units can idle cores at a batch tail (long deals block the batch); accepted per the issue, batches stay at today's sizes and arms still use rayon's pool inside `play_forks`.
- File line order is completion order, hence insignificant: every read sorts by deal, and tests compare sorted lines; only tally/duel/record output (deal-ordered) is byte-compared.
- Finished save skips the identity game, trusting the header: required by R850001's no-second-reads rule; the header's labels, infos, budget, and constants still bind the file to its agents.
- `duel_line` strings are stored, not recomputed, because they carry decision times; tally faults need saved `probe_faults` plus arm faults, both in the line, since the trunk is not replayed.

## Open questions

None; every behavior above is settled by the issue text.
```

3. Same file, `play_deal(game: &ArenaGame, probe: Probe) -> anyhow::Result<DealLine>`: run `play_game_probed`, build the one deal's jobs, run existing `play_forks` (keeps `(deal, fork, pair, arm)` assembly), flatten outcomes to `SavedArm` in slot order, then `duel: duel_line(outcome, replays(outcome)?)`, `record: game_record(outcome)?`, `hash: outcome.hash`. Extract the cand/ctl win-count loop from `play_forks` into `fn edge_of_slots(won: &[bool]) -> f64` and reuse it in `edges_of` (step 5) so saved and live edges cannot diverge.
4. Same file, file I/O: `append_deal_line(path, line)` opens with append+create, writes one JSON line, flushes. `load_save(path)` reads the header plus deal lines into a `BTreeMap<i32, DealLine>`; a last line that fails to parse is dropped with an `eprintln` warning (the torn line); a failing non-last line or a duplicate deal number is an error naming the line. `check_header(header, args, a, b, budget, deals)` compares set, games, extend, budget, `FORK_ROLLOUTS`, `FORK_MAX_PER_GAME`, catalog version, both labels and both agent infos, bailing with the differing field's name (e.g. `"arena: save <file> is for --games 200, not 400"`).
5. Same file, resume core: `identity_check(game, probe, saved)` plays the first saved deal's trunk and bails naming `trunk hash` or `forks` unless hash and every fork's seat, `at_move`, and both actions' `fork_key` match. `edges_of(lines in deal order) -> Vec<ForkEdge>` recomputes edges from saved arms. `tally_from_lines(header, lines) -> (String tally_json, Vec<String> duel_lines, Vec<GameRecord>)` via existing `fork_tally`, in deal order. `next_batch(games_done, live, extend, initial_deals) -> Option<(first, len)>`: first batch `(1, initial_deals)`; later batches only when `extend`, `None` when `screen_done(live, games_done)`, else `(games_done+1, min(SCREEN_EXTEND_DEALS, SCREEN_MAX_GAMES-games_done))`. `--extend` totals count saved plus new deals together.
6. Same file, `resume_save(path, expected: &SaveHeader, base: &str, b: &Entrant, initial_deals, extend, make_probe: &dyn Fn(&ArenaGame) -> anyhow::Result<Probe>) -> anyhow::Result<SaveReport>`: load, `check_header`, finished check (every target deal present, and with `extend` also `screen_done`), returning a re-read of the file with zero games played when finished; else `identity_check` on the first saved deal, then per-batch `par_iter` over missing deals calling `play_deal`, appending each finished line immediately under a file mutex with flush (completion order; readers sort by deal), looping on `next_batch`. `SaveReport` carries tally JSON, duel lines, records, and a games-played count.

Same file, `run()`: after the existing arg checks and entrant setup, branch on `args.save`. `None`: today's loop verbatim. `Some(path)`: build the expected header (budget = `AI_GATE_BUDGET`, the trunk setups' budget; deals = requested count), create-or-resume the file (write header when creating), call `resume_save` with `|game| Probe::for_game(&args.a, game.self_budget, game.n)`, then print duel lines, tally, and a `"<n> deals in <file>"` line to stdout exactly like the `--out` branch minus record appending (the save file is the record store; never re-append records). Ruling + docs: write `spec/rulings/R4607000.md` (`cards: "§9.9, R4397000, R850001, R4319000, R1489000, issue #4607"`, Hearthstone-has-no-counterpart line as R4397000 does) and `spec/pending/4607.md` (the `**[[R4607000]] … (issue #4607, …)**` paragraph). `training/improve.md` `### A screen`, after the fork-screen paragraph: pass `--save` at a path inside the worktree, rerun the same command after a cut, record the tally in the knob's config comment, delete the file before finishing.
